title: Ayyub's spring
hook: strike the ground with your foot: a cool spring to wash and drink (38:41–44)

segments.voice: Yesterday, fitna, Dawud's test in the two brothers' dispute,, and your line was judge, then look at yourself. Did you give the other side a voice before deciding? Day five hundred fifty-six.

A hot afternoon, years of illness behind you, your body aching, and someone hands you a glass of cold water. You drink it slowly. Then you splash some on your face, the back of your neck, your wrists. For a moment, that's everything. Back in Surah Al-Anbiya, we heard Ayyub's cry: harm has touched me, and You are the most merciful. Surah Sad tells what happened next, and the answer to years of suffering arrives in the most ordinary form there is. Water. Under his own feet.

Surah Sad, verse forty-one. Remember Our servant Ayyub, when he called his Lord: Satan has touched me with weariness and torment. Then verse forty-two, the answer, as a command: urkud bi-rijlik, strike the ground with your foot. And there it is: a spring. Cool water to wash in, and to drink. Notice that he has to do something. Not much. One stamp of a weak foot. But the healing comes through that small act, and through water, the plainest gift of all. Verse forty-three: and We gave him back his family, and as many again with them, a mercy from Us and a reminder for those with understanding. Then a stranger detail. Verse forty-four: take a bundle of grass in your hand and strike with it, and don't break your oath. Commentators explain that during his illness Ayyub had sworn to strike someone, many say his wife, a set number of times. Allah gave him a gentle way to keep his word without harming her: one tap with a bundle of stalks. Mercy for him, and mercy for her. And then the verdict: We found him patient. How excellent a servant! He was always turning back. There's a hadith in Bukhari that adds one more picture. After his healing, while Ayyub was bathing, a shower of golden locusts fell, and he began gathering them. His Lord called: didn't I make you rich enough? And Ayyub answered: yes, but I can never do without Your blessing. Patient in the long hardship, and still grateful for every small gift after it.
screen: `A COOL SPRING TO WASH AND DRINK.`
`A BUNDLE OF GRASS, AN OATH KEPT.`

segments.voice: The practice: wash your face with cool water. If you can, go to a sink now. Let the water run cold. Cup it in your hands, and wash your face slowly, once, twice, three times. Feel it on your forehead, your eyes, your cheeks. If you can't get up, picture it in detail. Then sit, damp-faced, and think of Ayyub's spring: the answer to years of waiting, in the plainest gift there is. The bell holds the time.
Ayyub's spring. After long illness, Ayyub is told to strike the ground with his foot, and a cool spring rises for washing and drinking. Today's word.

Your line: patient; a spring came. Today, when something has been hard for a long time, take one small step, one stamp of the foot, and watch for the ordinary gift that answers. Day five hundred fifty-six.

howItsDone: Muslims hold up Ayyub as the model of sabr, patience in illness and loss; his cry in 21:83 is often recited by the sick, and his story is told to comfort those in long hardship.

original.note: Arabic: strike (the ground) with your foot (38:42).

trapdoor: what you thought: Ayyub was patient, so he got better.
what it means: after long illness he is told to take one small step, and the cure comes through plain water.
what a scholar hears: 38:41–44 adds the bundle of grass (dighth) and the verdict 'We found him patient'; Bukhari 279 has the golden locusts and his reply that he can't do without Allah's blessing.
